t.6.98.1: Hearing that Rāvaṇa had been slain by the great-souled Rāghava, the rākṣasī women, worn down by grief, rushed out from the inner apartments.
t.6.98.2: Though restrained again and again, they rolled about in the dust of the earth, their hair loosened, tormented by grief, like cows whose calves have been slain.
t.6.98.3: Going out by the northern gate together with the rākṣasas, they entered the dreadful battlefield, searching for their slain husband.
t.6.98.4: Crying out "O noble son!" and "Alas, my lord!" on every side, they fell down upon the earth, which was marked with headless trunks and become a mire of blood.
t.6.98.5: Those women, their eyes brimming with tears, overcome by grief for their husbands, cried out, wailing like she-elephants whose herd-leader has been slain.
t.6.98.6: They saw Rāvaṇa, of mighty body, great valour and great splendour, lying slain upon the ground, resembling a heap of dark collyrium.
t.6.98.7: Suddenly seeing their husband lying in the dust of the battlefield, they fell upon his limbs like forest creepers that have been cut down.
t.6.98.8: Out of deep esteem, one of them embraced him and wept; another clasped his feet, and another wept clinging to his neck.
t.6.98.9: One woman, flinging up her arms, rolled about on the ground; another, seeing the face of the slain one, fell into a swoon.
t.6.98.10: One woman, placing his head in her lap, wept as she gazed upon his face, bathing that face with her tears as a lotus is bathed with dewdrops.
t.6.98.11: Thus stricken, seeing their lord Rāvaṇa slain upon the ground, they cried out in many ways from grief, and again they lamented.
t.6.98.12: He by whom Śakra was terrified, by whom Yama was terrified, by whom King Vaiśravaṇa was deprived of the Puṣpaka.
t.6.98.13: He who struck great fear into the Gandharvas, the ṛṣis and the high-souled gods, he now lies here on the battlefield, slain.
t.6.98.14: He who knew no fear from asuras or from suras, nor likewise from serpents, now faces this fear from a man.
t.6.98.15: He who could not be slain by the gods, nor likewise by the Dānavas and Rākṣasas, now lies here on the battlefield, slain by a man fighting on foot.
t.6.98.16: He who could not be slain by the gods, nor by the Yakṣas, nor likewise by the Asuras, this very one, like some creature void of strength, has been brought to death by a mortal.
t.6.98.17: Speaking thus in many ways, those women of his wept; and, afflicted with grief, they lamented yet more, again and again.
t.6.98.18: But because you would not listen to your friends, who always spoke for your good, these women of yours, we ourselves, and your own self have now all alike been brought to ruin.
t.6.98.19: Even though your beloved brother Vibhīṣaṇa spoke words for your good, he was insolently reviled by you out of delusion, you who longed for your own destruction.
t.6.98.20: If Sītā of Mithilā had been returned by you to Rāma, this terrible and great calamity, which destroys us to the very root, would not have befallen us.
t.6.98.21: Then his brother would have had his wish fulfilled, Rāma would have become an ally to our house, and all of us would not be widows; our desires would be fulfilled, and there would be no enemies.
t.6.98.22: But you, cruel one, by holding Sītā captive by force, have brought down all three alike: the rākṣasas, us, and yourself.
t.6.98.23: O bull among rākṣasas, neither acting at will nor desire is truly yours; fate sets everything in motion, and whoever is slain is slain by fate.
t.6.98.24: This destruction of the vānaras and of your rākṣasas in battle, and of you as well, O mighty-armed one, has come about through the working of fate.
t.6.98.25: Neither by wealth nor by desire, neither by valor nor by command, can the course of fate, once it has been set in motion, be turned back in this world.
t.6.98.26: Thus lamented those wretched wives of the lord of the Rākṣasas, afflicted with grief like female ospreys, their eyes clouded with tears.
